title: Why repricing shares can settle investor fraud
why: Repricing preferred shares to the valuation full disclosure would have implied compensates investors defrauded by undisclosed material facts.

title: Why languages moved from UTF-16 to UTF-8 strings
why: Two-byte encodings assumed 65536 characters and wasted space; UTF-8 wins on size and C interop, with separate byte and codepoint APIs.

title: Hidden costs of splitting a monolith into microservices
why: JSON serialization between services adds real latency, and coordinating branches, builds, rollbacks and auth across many repos becomes hard.

title: Why skipping grades may cost growing-up time
why: Entering college two years younger left the author less ready for early decisions; a gap year of real experience may serve teens better.

title: Why photo startups move off AWS at scale
why: AWS optimizations on S3, EC2 and RDS cut costs, and large photo platforms usually run their own storage and servers, reportedly far cheaper.

title: Critique of Snopes relying on an unsupported claim
why: Author says a debunking used a false amputation claim that a podiatrist contradicted; the argument is about the editorial process, not a lesson.

title: Assertion that non-ionising radiation dogma is wrong
why: Asserts the scientific consensus is dogma without specific mechanisms or evidence; it is a credibility argument, not an explanation.

title: Moderator list of related Reddit protest threads
why: A context-bound list of linked threads that only makes sense inside the Apollo story; not informational on its own.

title: Cowboy versus architect programmer personas
why: Opinion-driven taxonomy and criticism of agile; it asserts preferences rather than explaining a mechanism a reader could apply.

title: Opinion on cancellation and workplace speech
why: Political argument about speech, employment and partisan politics with no technical or informational lesson.

title: Opinion that US healthcare is a consumer product
why: Political opinion comparing US and European health systems, mostly rhetorical with no verified mechanism.

title: Moderator defends self against bootcamp accusations
why: Defensive response in a specific dispute about a company and subreddit; only meaningful in that context.

title: Complaint about large iPhones and Apple product direction
why: Emotional product rant and finance-versus-product speculation with no verifiable lesson for the reader.

title: Argument that Apple is a counterexample to hacker culture
why: Opinion-based debate about company culture and pg's essay, with no concrete insight to take away.

title: The typical academic career trajectory and its finances
why: Scientists often spend years in training and low-paid postdocs, then face tenure denial around age 44 with few alternatives.

title: Argument that stopping money requires punishment
why: Philosophical argument about commune failures and incentives; persuasive opinion rather than a documented explanation.

title: Complaint about CNN clickbait and opinion mixing
why: Opinion criticism of a news outlet and Reddit-driven news judgment, without evidence or lasting technical lesson.

title: Why cars beat transit on latency and flexibility
why: Cars win on zero wait, proportional lateness penalty, night and weather availability, and direct routing; transit must match these to shift traffic.

title: Complaint about hard coding interviews at FAANG
why: Anecdotal frustration with interview difficulty and interviewers; expresses grievance without a transferable insight.

title: Reversed composite index order made inserts far slower
why: Same data with reversed index column order took 37+ hours to load versus 25 minutes, with identical checksums, showing index layout drives insert cost.

title: Automatic scale tracking makes weight loss easier
why: Automatic logging and trend-line graphs reveal progress hidden by daily noise and avoid fear-driven abandonment of manual tracking.

title: Opinion on journalists and Portland protest reporting
why: Political argument about media bias and protest coverage; the claims are not substantiated in a way that teaches anything.

title: Employer tax and labor-law exposure from remote staff abroad
why: Companies face tax and local employment-law liability when staff work from another country, and not knowing where an employee lives is no defense.

title: Personal account of trial-by-fire onboarding
why: Self-congratulatory story about sink-or-swim hiring; mostly personal reflection with limited transferable knowledge.

title: Skepticism about scientific method and brain theories
why: Opinion critique of researchers' pet theories with loosely connected examples; argument rather than explanation.

title: Speculation on FCC authority over rogue satellites
why: A list of open questions and speculation about regulation and cubesats; no settled explanation is offered.

title: Opinion on why maintainers feel unpaid
why: Reflective commentary on open source burnout and expectations; sympathetic but offers no concrete mechanism or guide.

title: How DynamoDB maps keys to replicated quorum groups
why: Hash keys map to 3-replica quorum groups with a master for writes, and the storage layer was sharded MySQL instances rather than LevelDB.

title: Personal account of being scammed by a startup
why: Narrative of a failed startup and missing payroll; a grievance story with no technical or general lesson.

title: Argument that bitcoin adoption implies monetary collapse
why: Logical critique of bitcoin believers that is argumentative and opinion-driven rather than explanatory.

title: Running a large data platform on Nix, not containers
why: Containers give reproducible deployments but not builds; Nix also makes builds reproducible, while stateful databases are the hard part Kubernetes does not solve.

title: Essay on hackers as the new privileged class
why: Rhetorical argument about class and counterculture, sharply worded and largely opinion.

title: Why word processors need custom text layout beyond the DOM
why: Selection in mixed bidi text and fast line-level reflow need layout information the DOM does not expose, which explains canvas rendering.

title: Critique of YC equity deals and VC access
why: Opinion about the economics of accelerators and valuation hype, presented as argument rather than explanation.

title: AlphaGo maximizes win probability, so boards look deceptively even
why: Playing for win probability rather than points can keep positions looking balanced to humans while Sedol's odds quietly fall; an edge-instantiation example.

title: Sneering critique of a Plan 9 desktop guide
why: Snarky dismissal of retrocomputing with few concrete technical facts about Plan 9 itself.

title: Why banks keep legacy systems with weak password storage
why: Vendor legacy systems cannot retrofit salted hashes easily, so banks rely on second factors, network isolation and law enforcement rather than risky rewrites.

title: Opinion that Vue is for beginners
why: Strong framework preference with one anecdote; opinion dominates and the concrete JSX example is too thin to teach a general lesson.

title: Wait before extracting repeated code into helpers
why: Early extraction produces helpers full of options; let duplication stand through several changes, then refactor once real shared patterns emerge.

title: SR-71 engineering: leaks, refueling and maintenance tradeoffs
why: The SR-71 leaked fuel on the ground so panels could seal in flight and needed refueling after takeoff; great designs are what they need to be.

title: Essay on why aviation and computing stalled
why: Broad essay with historical framing and speculation about limits; opinion-driven rather than a precise explanation.

title: Incremental grading, not grade levels, drives academic stress
why: Small weighted assignments make every test high-stakes, while a single final exam allows learning; grade inflation adds panic.

title: Practical sleep habits ranked by impact
why: Consistent bedtime and wake time matter most, then morning outdoor light, dim evenings, passive pre-bed routines and nasal breathing.

title: Insider view of how Optimizely lost its self-serve base
why: Abandoning self-serve for opaque enterprise sales and squeezing clients eroded culture and value, while hype metrics hid the decline.

title: Argument that inequality is not inherently bad
why: Political-economic opinion about wealth and fairness; argumentative with no technical or verifiable insight to keep.

title: Opinion on coding tests and AI assistants
why: Reflective opinion about grading and interviews, with no concrete explanation or resources.

title: Complaint about a cracked Samsung laptop screen
why: Personal product complaint and brand comparison without a generalizable technical lesson.

title: Opinion on Twitter verification and product judgment
why: Commentary on a product change and analogies to Stack Overflow; opinion rather than substantive explanation.

title: Employee defends company's performance-first approach
why: Company rationale and self-justification for a product direction; persuasive framing rather than an independent explanation.

title: Latency tradeoffs among HLS, DASH, WebRTC and MJPEG
why: HLS and DASH sit around seven seconds of latency, WebRTC is hard to productize, while MJPEG gives sub-second latency at the cost of compression.

title: Simple earplugs beat expensive noise-cancelling headphones
why: Roughly ten-dollar silicone earplugs block noise far better than $200 noise-cancelling headphones, according to this long-time user.

title: Opinion on honest airline pricing and short flights
why: Policy advocacy with a hypothetical advertising wish list; persuasive opinion rather than verified evidence.

title: Complaints and open questions about text encodings
why: Frustrated list of unanswered questions about BOMs and bidi text, with no answers offered.

title: Spreadsheet-driven cuts eroded company culture and morale
why: Optimizing what is easy to quantify, like benefits, while ignoring hard-to-measure morale effects damaged culture; measurement is not understanding.

title: What makes API reference pages scannable
why: Group methods into sections, align signatures, use color and provide per-section summaries so readers can scan instead of facing text blobs.

title: Personal reflection on living cheaply and working less
why: Lifestyle anecdote about low spending and happiness; personal and not a transferable lesson.

title: Skeptical complaint about Rust package manager
why: Opinion about platform priorities and Ruby tooling, with no concrete technical explanation.

title: Rant about macOS bugs and slow command-line tools
why: Emotional list of frustrations without diagnosis or fix; complaint rather than explanation.

title: Why isolated browsers break screen reader support
why: Rendering pages inert for security strips the DOM semantics screen readers rely on, so accessibility is hard to retrofit across dynamic web pages.

title: Reflection on non-jokes and poetry slam delivery
why: Reflective essay about humor and performance; interesting but not an explanation a reader can apply or verify.

title: Have GPT-3 write parenthetical reasoning before answering
why: Asking for an internal monologue in parentheses before the answer improved accuracy and let the model reject nonsense questions.

title: Why Chinese firms function as tools of statecraft
why: State, military and corporations are entangled across industries in China, so comparing Huawei to Western competitors misreads its role.

title: Lament about the web's loss of open standards
why: Nostalgic opinion about walled gardens and chat standards with no technical explanation or concrete takeaway.

title: Flat Lorentzian space cannot be hyperbolic space
why: Minkowski space has zero curvature, so it cannot be constant negative curvature hyperbolic space; the Lorentz group acts as isometries of H^n instead.

title: Reflection on bakery work and abstract office jobs
why: Personal essay about job satisfaction and physicality; a sentiment rather than an explanation a reader could learn from.

title: Worry about income growth lagging house prices
why: Personal worry backed by selected figures and a trend argument; advocacy rather than a rigorous, self-contained explanation.

title: Complaint about tall passengers and economy seats
why: Personal frustration about airline seat pitch and pricing; no technical lesson and mostly grievance.

title: Why Munich's LiMux migration struggled beyond Linux
why: Problems came from very old desktop hardware, slow SDSL site links and office software gaps, not only from the Linux desktop itself.

title: Personal account of cheap live-in staff abroad
why: Lifestyle anecdote about hiring staff and comfort abroad; personal experience with little transferable knowledge.

title: What makes SaaS demos fail for technical buyers
why: Evaluators want live feature demos, technical answers, relevant use cases and clear security details; slides and vague claims destroy trust.

title: Why many patents describe obvious implementations
why: Examiners' obviousness checks focus on combining existing claims, so patents for routine engineering implementations get granted despite skilled practitioners.

title: Frustrated customer threatens to leave Apple ecosystem
why: Opinion about platform trust and a wish for an alternative; no concrete technical explanation of the behavior.

title: Personal account of living homeless in a van
why: Emotional first-person narrative about stigma and harassment; affecting but without a lesson a curious technical reader can apply.

title: Knuth versus McIlroy: the word-frequency critique in context
why: Bentley's column asked Knuth to write a literate program for word frequency; McIlroy's review was unfair to the program he was asked to write.

title: Speculation that AI will eliminate most software jobs
why: Predictive opinion about labor and market correction without evidence or mechanism; speculation rather than explanation.

title: Argument that community mattered more than the software
why: Opinion about open source community and takedowns; argumentative commentary on one project's situation.

title: Collapsing the stack with UDP, kernel bypass and mmap caching
why: One process replaced database, cache and auth tiers; it used UDP with NaCl crypto, bypassed the kernel, and cached reads via LMDB memory mapping.

title: Matt Cutts responds to a webmaster appeal
why: Company-specific response to one complaint about AdWords and appeals; procedural news rather than a reusable lesson.

title: Anecdotes about punch cards and early debugging
why: Reminiscence about old workflows and media attitudes; personal nostalgia rather than a clear explanation a reader can apply.

title: Screwdriver analogy arguing against copyleft framing
why: Argumentative essay rebutting an article on free software; persuasive opinion, not a mechanism or verifiable fact.

title: Quote on ignoring history in technology
why: Reflective opinion about history and a person's business conduct; essayistic rather than informational.

title: Defense of iBooks Author EULA revenue terms
why: Argument that restrictions are the price of a free tool; opinion on licensing ethics rather than a technical explanation.

title: Why industrial control networks need data diodes
why: SCADA links often use two-way protocols where only software enforces one-way flow; hardware data diodes physically block backflow from IT networks.

title: Humorous take on big consultancies and legacy IT
why: Satirical generalization about consultants and corporate IT; entertaining but anecdotal rather than instructive.

title: Essay on comfortable societies losing drive
why: Sweeping historical opinion about complacency and generations; a thesis without evidence a reader can check.

title: Opinion favoring static types over dynamic languages
why: Preference argument about type checking and tooling; personal taste with some general points but no decisive evidence.

title: Google engineer defends AngularDart and Dart
why: Insider defense of how Google projects start, but it is mainly an argument against critics rather than a teachable explanation.

title: How a fake camera support call tried to extract payment
why: After an Amazon transfer, a caller asked for device serial numbers, claimed a virus and demanded $300 for an on-site visit; a useful warning pattern.

title: Argument that consumers should own dependency risk
why: Opinionated liability argument with a reference to consulting practice; a position statement rather than a how-to explanation.

title: Argument that robotaxis will fix congestion
why: Speculative policy argument with hypothetical pricing and unverified claims about future transport demand.

title: Wish for a paid Linux distribution
why: Speculative product wish and funding opinion; no concrete mechanism or evidence that the model would work.

title: Costs of bootstrapping a startup on personal savings
why: Bootstrapping consumed savings and years of career progress; founders should weigh their own savings as an investment before choosing it.

title: Learn ML by modifying working GitHub code
why: Pick a concrete problem, run existing code, experiment, and study theory only when a concept blocks you; courses are secondary.

title: Personal reflection on life after leaving work
why: Lifestyle reflection on following interests and happiness; personal experience with no concrete, transferable technique.

title: Meta-commentary on space feature article formula
why: Observation about narrative structure in space journalism; a critique of writing style, not technical knowledge.

title: Argument that debt forgiveness harms lending
why: Speculative economic argument predicting consequences of Croatia's debt cancellation; opinion rather than established evidence.

title: Argument for public drug research and low margins
why: Political argument about pharmaceutical economics; advocacy with some sourced points but mostly position-taking.

title: Skeptical take on Snowden's claims and motives
why: Opinion on a political figure's conduct and credibility, with no technical or verifiable lesson.

title: Rebuttal of complaints about Rust benchmarking and casts
why: Argumentative rebuttal of a critique of Rust; some points about explicit casts, but mostly debate rather than a lesson.

title: Proposal for a tech-funded anti-troll legal fund
why: Advocacy proposal with speculative funding figures and no evidence that the scheme would work.
